meta.tagline: A peninsula of wind, mastic and stone streets

overview.title: Welcome to Cesme
overview.intro: The Cesme peninsula is the westernmost tip of the Turkish Aegean, and here the wind is not weather — it's identity: it turned the old windmills, it snaps the surf flags, it cools Alacati's stone streets in summer. On one side, bougainvillea-draped stone houses and wild-herb mezes; on the other, the Caribbean-colored shallows of Ilica and a marina in the shadow of a castle. Across the water sits the silhouette of the Greek island of Chios — half an hour by ferry. This peninsula is small, but its days are long: morning market, noon cove, afternoon sea breeze, night on the stone streets.

local_word.definition: The cool afternoon sea breeze of the Aegean: Cesme summer's invisible air conditioning. Ask a local 'is there imbat today?' — the answer is both a weather report and an evening plan. When the imbat blows, the stone streets cool down and the tables move outdoors.

rules.title: Make the wind your planning partner
rules.description: On this peninsula the wind is the boss of the day: the poyraz that thrills surfers will flip a beach umbrella. Choose your cove by the wind — on a windy day the Alacati surf bay is a spectacle, and sheltered Pasalimani is your refuge.

rules.title: Live Alacati at morning and night, flee to a cove at noon
rules.description: The stone streets belong to crowds at noon, photographers at dawn, and dinner tables at night. When everyone is at the coves in the midday heat, be there too — Alacati shows its best face early and late.

rules.title: Meet the herbs and the mastic where they live
rules.description: Cesme's kitchen starts at the wild-herb stall and ends with mastic: don't leave without seeing şevketibostan or tasting mastic pudding. April's Alacati Herb Festival is this cuisine's official holiday — if your dates align, build your program around it.

quick_facts.label: Signature
quick_facts.sub: A stop on the world surf calendar

tip.label: The Cesme philosophy
tip.text: The peninsula sets its clock by the wind, not the sun: calm mornings belong to the sea, the afternoon imbat belongs to the table. Check the wind rose before you plan — that's what a Cesme local does.

transport.title: Getting Around the Peninsula
transport.intro: A motorway links Izmir to the peninsula in under an hour; inside, dolmus minibuses weave the Cesme–Alacati–Ilica triangle, and the far coves call for a steering wheel.

items.title: Arriving from Izmir
items.description: One hour from Adnan Menderes Airport on the motorway: airport transfers and buses run steadily. Intercity buses to Cesme's bus station leave Izmir at all hours.

items.title: The dolmus triangle
items.description: Minibuses shuttle all day between Cesme center, Alacati and Ilica: cheap and practical. Night returns run late in season — asking the time of the last dolmus is still good Aegean manners.

items.title: A car for cove-hunting
items.description: Dolmus service to far corners like Altinkum, Pirlanta and Ildiri is sparse: cove-hopping calls for a rental car or scooter. On summer weekends, parking inside Alacati tests your patience — leave the car outside and walk.

items.title: The Chios ferry
items.description: The ferry from Cesme harbor to Chios takes half an hour: bring your passport, go in the morning, return in the evening. Greek coffee, mastika liqueur and lanes that echo old Aegean towns — the peninsula's shortest trip abroad.

items.title: Bikes and e-scooters
items.description: Inner Alacati and the Ilica seafront are made for pedaling: flat, scenic and pleasant. Factor in the midday heat and the evening wind — the morning ride always wins.

callout.label: Ferry tip
callout.text: Do Chios on a Saturday: cross on the morning ferry, wander the Kampos mansions of Chios town, buy your mastic gifts from the village shops, sail back in the evening. Passport + early booking — summer sailings fill up.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: The peninsula's choice is a triangle: Alacati's stone hotels, Ilica's beach, Cesme center's marina — plus quiet Dalyan for those who want calm.

local_word.definition: Alacati's houses of local sandstone with blue-green shutters: the legacy of Greek master builders. Most are boutique hotels today — their thick walls stay cool in summer, and their courtyards are breakfast's most beautiful stage.

items.name: Alacati
items.description: Courtyard boutique hotels inside the stone streets: breakfast in the garden, evenings at street tables. Busy and pricey on summer weekends — but this is the capital of atmosphere.

items.name: Ilica
items.description: The peninsula's beach classic with white sand and warm, shallow sea: thermal springs bubble up right at the shore. Perfect for families and long beach days — ten minutes to the center by dolmus.

items.name: Cesme center
items.description: Hotels around the castle, marina and bazaar: the ferry pier and bus station at hand. A sensible base for exploring the whole peninsula.

items.name: Dalyan (Cesme)
items.description: A hushed neighborhood of fishing boats and canal-side fish restaurants: quayside tables at night, stillness by day. Away from the crowds, close to the sea.

items.name: Pasalimani & Ayayorgi side
items.description: Boutique hotels above sheltered coves, with beach clubs as neighbors: turquoise by day, clinking glasses by night. Protected from the wind — for those who want to wake up on the water.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Cesme's calendar opens with the herb festival and closes with September gold; July–August is windy and full, winter is calm and true.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Herb Festival Spring
items.subtitle: Spring · Herb stalls, blossoming stone streets
items.description: April is the holiday of the herbs: at the Alacati Herb Festival the stalls drown in green, from şevketibostan to wild fennel. In May–June the sea warms and the streets are still uncrowded — the peninsula's most elegant window.

callout.label: April tip
callout.text: If the Herb Festival falls on your weekend, book your room months ahead: the whole Aegean shows up. Do your stall tour in the morning — the crowds peak in the afternoon.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Wind and Stage
items.subtitle: Summer · Surf flags, full coves, Izmir weekend influx
items.description: The surf bays fill with sails, the beach clubs build their stages, and Izmir moves to the peninsula on weekends. The sea is clear, the wind is lively, the prices are at their peak — plan around the Friday–Sunday traffic.

callout.label: Weekend note
callout.text: On summer Saturdays the Izmir–Cesme motorway and inner Alacati fill up: arrive Thursday and leave Monday, or build your program on weekdays. The same coves are half as busy midweek.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: September Gold
items.subtitle: Autumn · Warm sea, empty stone streets
items.description: September is the peninsula's finest month: the sea holds its summer warmth, the coves are calm, Alacati's tables are easy. October carries on with grape harvest and quiet beach days — this is the connoisseur's season.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: Come in mid-September: Altinkum's Caribbean water is empty, tables in Alacati need no haggling, the surf schools are relaxed. Summer prices have retreated too — the peninsula's two smartest weeks.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Quiet Peninsula
items.subtitle: Winter · Stone-street silence, thermal warmth
items.description: In winter the peninsula returns to its locals: Alacati quiets down, the market stalls fill with wild herbs and mandarins, and Ilica's thermal water stays warm even in the cold. On a stormy day, watching the sea is a program in itself.

callout.label: February tip
callout.text: On a winter weekend, go to the Alacati market, gather the season's greens from the herb stalls, and walk the stone streets without the crowds. The Alacati you can't see in summer — the real one — lives in this season.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Cesme table is set with two words: herbs and mastic — a kumru slips in between, seafood sits alongside, and the imbat blows over it all.

local_word.definition: The sandwich that carries Cesme's name: kasar cheese, sucuk sausage and tomato in a special sesame roll. The original is simple, its fame has spread to Izmir — the debate over the 'real Cesme kumru' is the peninsula's national sport.

items.name: Cesme kumru
items.description: Sesame bread, melted kasar, sucuk: a warm balance of three. The post-beach standing classic — the argument between 'extra sucuk' and 'plain cheese' people never ends, so try both.

items.name: Wild herb meze spread
items.description: Şevketibostan, sea beans, wild fennel, cibes greens: Aegean herbs meeting olive oil are the stars of the meze fridge. Order whatever the season gave — the herb table doesn't do scripts.
items.tag: From the meze fridge · season's pick

items.name: Fish in Dalyan
items.description: Catch of the day along the canal where the fishing boats tie up: sea bream, sea bass, dentex in season. At a quayside table with the sunset — choose from the display, ask the price before it hits the scale.
items.tag: On the canal quay · from the display

items.name: Mastic everything
items.description: Mastic pudding, mastic ice cream, mastic cookies and Turkish coffee with mastic: the resin of the island across the water is this coast's sweet signature. Have the pudding from a bakery, the ice cream on an evening stroll.
items.tag: Sweet signature · pudding from the bakery

items.name: Mastic artichoke season
items.description: In spring the peninsula's stalls turn to artichokes: braised in olive oil, grilled, or raw in salads. In the April–May window it's the star of every menu — don't miss its season.

items.name: Alacati breakfast
items.description: A spread breakfast in a stone courtyard: village cheeses, sautéed wild greens, mastic jam and griddle borek. The long ritual of a weekend morning — table in the shade, tea well-steeped, hurrying forbidden.
items.tag: In a stone courtyard · weekend ritual

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: On Alacati's busiest lanes, menu prices are stage prices: a back street or Cesme center sets the same table at a friendlier number. With herb mezes the measure is freshness — don't insist anywhere that won't show you the fridge.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone knows Alacati's main street; these six are the peninsula's hidden face.

items.rarity: Seaside village with an ancient theater
items.name: Ildiri (Erythrai)
items.description: A quiet village at the peninsula's northern tip, built over ancient Erythrai: island views from the theater ruins, a small fishing pier below. A silent sunset classic the crowds never reach.

items.name: Germiyan
items.description: A calm inland village of stone houses and vineyards: it comes alive on weekends with village breakfasts and a handicraft market. Alacati as it was twenty years ago — authentic and unhurried.

items.name: Ayayorgi Cove
items.description: A sheltered, pine-shaded cove of turquoise water: almost private in the early morning, shifting to beach-club rhythm in the afternoon. Both moods are lovely — go knowing the hour.

items.name: Altinkum
items.description: Fine white sand and transparent shallows: the peninsula's clearest beach. Wavy on a windy day, mirror-flat in the morning — bring your umbrella, settle for the simple beach shack, enjoy the wildness.

items.name: The Chios escape
items.description: Half an hour by ferry to Chios: mastic villages, the Genoese-patterned stone houses of Pyrgi, and quiet Greek tavernas. The Aegean's easiest day trip abroad — passport required.

items.name: Alacati surf bay at dawn
items.description: Go to the surf bay early: as the wind wakes, sails slip into the water one by one and the schools give their first lessons. Even with no plans to surf, take your coffee and watch from the jetty — the peninsula's most dynamic view.

callout.label: Cove strategy
callout.text: Choosing a cove in Cesme means reading the wind: on a poyraz day, sheltered Ayayorgi and Pasalimani; on a calm morning, Altinkum and Pirlanta. The peninsula is small — switching coves by the wind is a half-hour job.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: In summer Cesme is Izmir's showcase; know the showcase games and you'll live the peninsula at friendly prices.

items.name: Alacati main-street prices
items.description: In some venues on the busiest stone lanes, prices multiply with an atmosphere tax; even breakfast can land on the stage tariff.
items.instead: A back street, Germiyan village or Cesme center serves the same flavors at friendly numbers. Asking prices in Alacati isn't rude — not asking is expensive.

items.name: The beach club sunbed surprise
items.description: Some coves say 'free entry' and reveal the minimum spend later; a spot under an umbrella arrives at lunch-menu prices.
items.instead: Ask the minimum spend before you sit; Altinkum and the public beaches offer the same sea for the price of a towel. If you want the music cove, choose it knowingly.

items.name: Underestimating weekend traffic
items.description: On Saturday morning everyone leaving Izmir is on the same motorway; hunting for parking in Alacati becomes a patience test in the midday heat.
items.instead: Arrive Thursday, leave Monday; schedule cove-to-cove moves for the morning. Leaving the car outside Alacati and walking always wins.

items.name: Ignoring the wind
items.description: On a poyraz day at an exposed beach, umbrellas fly, the sea churns, and beach day becomes a struggle.
items.instead: Check the morning wind forecast: sheltered coves or surf-watching on windy days, open beaches on calm ones. The peninsula's rule is simple — don't fight the wind, plan with it.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Two things shape a plan in Cesme: the wind and the weekend. Check both before the calendar, and you'll live the peninsula's best self at half the price.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From stone streets to turquoise — a peninsula day

steps.title: Alacati morning
steps.description: Walk the stone streets while they're empty: shutters open, warm bread scents the air. Stretch the courtyard breakfast long — hurrying is forbidden.

steps.title: Cove shift — Altinkum
steps.description: First swim of the day in white sand and transparent shallows: morning is Altinkum's mirror hour.

steps.title: Kumru break
steps.description: Post-beach kumru eaten standing: the sesame bread warm, the cheese melted. Cold ayran on the side — a Cesme classic.

steps.title: Cesme center and the castle
steps.description: A marina stroll, gulf views from the castle walls, and a mastic ice cream break in the bazaar.

steps.title: Dalyan sunset
steps.description: Claim a table on the canal quay: order the day's fish as the boats come home — the imbat's coolness comes with the table.

steps.title: Night in Alacati
steps.description: Return to the stone streets: tables set out on the lanes, bougainvillea in the lamplight. Close with mastic pudding — a peninsula day ends sweet.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Coves, villages and an island — the full peninsula

steps.title: Classic Cesme
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: Alacati morning, Altinkum, kumru, the center, Dalyan.

steps.title: Wind and coves day
steps.description: Morning lesson or spectating at the surf bay; noon turquoise break at Ayayorgi; late afternoon at Ildiri for the ancient theater and pier silence; evening walk along the Ilica shore + a wild-herb meze dinner.

steps.title: Chios escape and farewell
steps.description: Morning ferry to Chios: Kampos mansions, mastic shops, lunch in a Greek taverna; evening return, and a promise of a farewell breakfast in Germiyan tomorrow — mastic jam in the suitcase.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: The Aegean accent is sweet, and the little word 'gari' is pure warmth; these five phrases open tables and conversations across the peninsula.

items.meaning: An Aegean-style welcome — the 'gari' tag is the seal of warmth
'Enjoy your meal' — opens and closes the herb table, you'll hear it after the meze fridge
'Health to your hands' — the finest thank-you to whoever cooked, kumru maker included
'How's the wind?' — the peninsula's weather question; the answer sets the day's plan
'Cheers!' — glasses rise as the imbat blows; the evening word of the Dalyan quay

checklist.title: Cesme Checklist
checklist.completion_message: Şerefe gari! You've lived the peninsula of wind the way it deserves!
